title: 2026-11-20 — A `#[path]` test child not named `*_tests.rs` is counted in its crate's coverage reading

data.head: ## 2026-11-20 — A `#[path]` test child not named `*_tests.rs` is counted in its crate's coverage reading

body:
The coverage leg leaves a unit-test file out of a crate's line reading by its name: a `#[path]` test module in a
`*_tests.rs` sibling is no record of the reading, but a child of that test module under any other name (a
`json_tests/fixtures.rs` holding fixture builders) is counted like source, so moving test code into it raises the
crate's figure with no product line changed.

Where it applies: any split that moves test helpers or fixtures out of a test module into a file of their own. Forecast
the crate's coverage reading with that file counted, or name the file `*_tests.rs` where it should stay out of the
reading.

title: 2026-11-20 — A child `mod` inside a `#[path]`-loaded test file resolves as from a `mod.rs`

data.head: ## 2026-11-20 — A child `mod` inside a `#[path]`-loaded test file resolves as from a `mod.rs`

body:
A test module loaded with `#[path = "x_tests.rs"]` is read as if it were a `mod.rs`, so a plain `mod fixtures;` inside
it looks for `fixtures.rs` beside it, not under `x_tests/`. Declare such a child with its own `#[path =
"x_tests/fixtures.rs"]`.
Where it applies: any out-of-line test module that gains a child module of its own.

A phase P5 control script that plants a host-path literal to prove a `/home/` probe reads red (a literal like
`/home/someone/x`) lands in the committed run dir, and `gate.py hygiene` P1 refuses it at the operator pass, costing a
respell and a re-fire there. Plant the control's literal in a form hygiene does not read as a host path — a
placeholder such as `/home/<user>/x` keeps the probe red and the run dir clean — from the first write.
Extended 2026-11-18: where hygiene still meets such a planted path, rewrite it to the `<user>` form and name it in
the card, without asking — the operator's standing ruling for this project.
Extended 2026-11-20: an evidence script that names the project root as a bare string literal reads P1 `in-root` too,
and `gate.py respell` refuses a bare root — have the script derive the root from its own path from the first write.
Extended 2026-11-19: the same `<user>` form holds for every control record a phase or implement run writes or quotes,
an outcome file included, not only a phase P5 control.

A code-health refactor: escher's own files over 800 code lines and functions over cognitive complexity 15 were split to meet the audit's bars. No behaviour changed.
Long functions were split into private helpers: the driver's command-line reading of its roles and address, the MCP server's run loop, the Dioxus runtime probe's walk, and three stand checks (the UI graph, actionable nodes, interactive names). Each check keeps its test name and its messages.
The snapshot model's unit tests moved whole out of line into their own test file. The driver's named key set moved whole into a child module of the command set and is re-exported under the same name. The wire-form tests' fixture builders moved into a test-only child.
No public item, signature, verb, field, span or log site changed. Every workspace test keeps its path (1631 listed, none gone, none new). The fast, coverage, stand-repeat (3 of 3 rounds green), a11y and doc legs are green, and CI is green on the final HEAD.
The founder ruled on F1 to F4: upstream's oversize files, its complex functions and its duplicated test pairs stay as upstream wrote them, and there is no route entry for escher's seven oversize integration-test targets.

body:
A codebase-health pass, refactor only: escher's own files over 800 code lines and functions over cognitive complexity 15 were split under those bars, and no behaviour changed.
No public item, signature, verb, field, span, log site, refusal or wire shape changed. No dependency, schema, config, CI job or gate changed, and nothing was retired.
The driver's Key enum (the closed key-name table) moved whole into a private child module and is re-exported unchanged. The command-line argv reader and the MCP server's run loop were each split into private helpers with the same behaviour.
The snapshot's unit tests and the driver JSON tests' fixture builders moved out of line into their own files, with no test name or body changed. Four stand checks had their bodies split into assert helpers.
Coverage was measured with every floor held: escher-driver went from 97.77 to 97.92 percent, dioxus-native-dom from 90.72 to 89.91 percent, and blitz-test-harness stayed at 96.07 percent.
The founder ruled that upstream-authored oversize files, upstream's complex functions and upstream's duplicated test pairs stay as upstream wrote them, and that no route entry is opened for escher's seven oversize integration-test targets.

the test-only fixture builders for the driver's JSON answer tests (caused items, findings, action nodes, layout explanation, graph), moved out of that test module
the driver's command schema and single command validation gate, covering the closed driver verb schema, the argument kinds and the target checks
the driver's closed key-name table (the Key enum with its ALL list, name and from_name), which the key argument kind and the --key flag are checked against
the snapshot reader, which reads each element's stable id, accessible name, state readings and masked control values into the snapshot
the snapshot's unit tests, covering accessible names, state readings, masked password and file values, range and select values, and the never-a-node rule for text runs, moved out of line
the escher-session command line, with the closed argv reader for the roles (serve, mcp, coverage) and the flags
the MCP server over stdio, which serves the driver's verbs as tools under bounded request lines and results
the Dioxus runtime probe test, which walks the virtual DOM's roots, listeners and dynamic nodes
the stand graph check, which checks that every graph node is a snapshot node, that no served id holds the reserved form, and that the declarations agree with the code
the stand actions check, which checks that each served screen lists its actionable nodes with the table's verbs
the stand accessibility check, which checks that every interactive-role element and region reads a name

The command line echoes nothing typed, and its usage and error messages: the reader that refuses bad argv was restructured but prints the same fixed texts with no caller input.

MCP server over stdio, with no print or panic and bounded request lines and results: its run loop was split into per-instance and per-session helpers. Transport, bounds, protocol errors and idle expiry are unchanged.

Closed driver verb schema, the single command validation gate and the key argument kind: the closed key-name table moved into its own private module and is re-exported. The set of key names and the --key flag are unchanged.

The snapshot's masked control values (password and file inputs masked, the MASKED_VALUE stand-in, the mask holding on every carrier): the tests that guard this mask moved out of line, unchanged, and still pass.
The snapshot's state readings and the snapshot text state words (selected, pressed, invalid, clickable, checked, disabled): the unit tests that guard these readings moved out of line unchanged.
Stable element id, the reserved separator form and no NodeId crossing: the stand graph check that guards these was split into assert helpers, with every assertion and message kept.
The actions answer (nodes, verbs, keyed) and the one actionable rule for both readings: the stand actions check that guards them was split into helpers, with its assertions kept.
Accessible-name exits and region naming: the stand accessibility check that guards them was split into helpers, with its assertions kept.

Per-crate line coverage floors: every crate stayed at or above its floor. escher-driver read 97.92 percent and dioxus-native-dom 89.91 percent. Name this only where a row's cell holds a floor or a reading.

cargo-llvm-cov as the coverage tool: a path-declared test child whose file name does not end in _tests.rs is counted in its crate's coverage reading. The JSON test fixtures child raised escher-driver by 0.15 points.
The JSON answer crossings (graph, actions, caused text, coverage answer): the fixture builders their serialization tests read moved into a test-only child module. No answer shape changed.
Dependency security, covering cargo-deny, licence gates, pins, locked builds and CI action pins: no dependency or manifest changed.
Secret management and environment variables: no secret, credential or environment read changed.
Data protection, covering the history database, HTTP cache, cookies, TLS and kept check files: nothing that stores or keeps data was reached.
Outbound HTTP, fetch methods, CORS and same-origin absences, iframe and import limits, and script fetchers: no network or engine-loading code was reached.
The session socket, its wire grammar, its replies, the recording directory and the state directory: no session host or socket code changed.
The telemetry sink, log target allowlists and span field contracts: no log site or span changed.
Authentication and authorization, CI token scopes and publish jobs: no CI workflow or publishing path changed.
Select lists, range inputs, password painting and the engine's event model: no engine or rendering behaviour changed. Only tests and helper structure moved.

body:
Codebase-health pass: our files over 800 code lines and our functions over cognitive 15 were brought under those bars by splitting them. No behaviour, public item, verb, field, span or log site changed, and no test was renamed (1631 test paths before and after, none gone, none new).
Unit-test modules moved out of line: the snapshot reader's tests now sit in a sibling test file declared by path, and the driver JSON tests' fourteen fixture builders moved to a fixtures child module. The driver's Key enum moved whole into a private child module, re-exported unchanged.
The command-line reader's role parsing, the MCP server's run loop, the dioxus runtime probe's tree walk and four stand integration checks were split into private helpers. The new stand assertion helpers are track_caller and keep their messages as written.
Measured: files over 800 went from 25 to 22 (ours 10 to 7, the seven left being integration-test targets; upstream's 15 unchanged). Functions over cognitive 15 went from 101 to 94 (ours 7 to 0; upstream's 94 unchanged). Coverage: escher-driver 97.77 to 97.92 %, dioxus-native-dom 90.72 to 89.91 %, blitz-test-harness 96.07 % unchanged, every crate at or above its floor.
The founder ruled on F1 to F4: upstream's oversize files, complex functions and duplicated test pairs are kept as upstream's, and escher's seven oversize integration-test targets are kept as they are, with no route entry.
All gates were green (fast, coverage, stand-repeat 3 of 3 rounds, a11y, doc), and CI was green 17/17 on the pre-CI commit.

The driver JSON tests gain a fixtures child module. This is a further exception to the inline rule.
Split test modules keep their paths: this session split two test modules and moved one test module out of line, and every test path held (1631 listed, 0 gone, 0 new). The rule is exercised and holds.

Cognitive-complexity ceiling read on the host: our functions over 15 went from 7 to 0, and upstream's 94 are kept by the founder's ruling F2. The row's statement that engine functions over the ceiling are left as they are is now the founder's own ruling.

Per-crate line coverage floors, and the coverage leg gated by them: the escher-driver reading rose to 97.92 % and the dioxus-native-dom reading fell to 89.91 %. Both stay at or above their floors. Where a row's cell holds a per-crate reading or floor value, it is touched.

One integration test target per behaviour and one target per file (blitz-tests): four stand checks and the runtime probe were edited in place, and no target was added, split or merged. The founder's ruling F4 keeps the seven oversize integration-test targets whole.

Shared test modules and shared stand tables in one module: the new stand assertion helpers stay private to each target and none moved into the shared stand modules. A row about where shared stand checks live should be weighed.
Test failures print no argument value, and call assertions carry a row index only: the new stand assertion helpers are track_caller and keep each message as written, with the index passed in.
Reserved owner-key id form: the stand graph check that no served id holds the reserved separator was moved into a helper, with its behaviour unchanged.
One actionable rule for both readers: the stand actions check that every actionable node is listed by both readers was moved into helpers.
Listeners read from the vdom walk: the runtime probe's walk over roots, listeners and dynamic nodes was split into three recursive helpers.

Driver verbs (the lookup and the verb table) and the driver argument kind for names: the Key enum and its key names moved into a private child module and are re-exported. No name, verb or argument kind changed.
Harness re-exports keyboard types: the driver's Key type moved module, but its public path stands. This is indirect.
escher-session command line contracts (command form, the host, mcp and coverage roles, refused line): the reader that parses them was split into helpers. No form, refusal or exit code changed.
MCP server and MCP role contracts (tools/list, protocol lines, stdout, refused input): the server's run loop was split into a per-instance and a per-session helper. No answer changed.
Snapshot node contracts (clickable, masked value, number) and the typed-password-never-returned decisions: the snapshot reader's tests that witness them moved out of line unchanged.
Stand checks repeated three rounds and the zero-failure budget for stand checks: stand-repeat read 3 of 3 rounds green over the edited stand checks.
Every requirement witnessed inside stand-repeat, and stand checks run in both layout modes: the edited stand checks keep their witnesses and modes.

Upstream's cdp-server and vibey-script duplicated test pairs are kept as upstream's, by the founder's ruling F3. The duplication reading is not held against them.
